cards.title: The culture surrounding 'ideal' childbirth has to evolve
cards.body: Letters respond to an article about a five-day labour, with an NHS doctor sharing her experience of feeling 'othered' during childbirth. The discussion highlights how cultural expectations around 'ideal' labour need to change.

cards.title: Parenting is hard. Should we let AI do it for us?
cards.body: Tech companies offer tools like eye-movement trackers and 'optimized nap predictions' for parents. The article questions whether these technologies are actually needed or simply exploit parental anxiety.

cards.title: Should I try the '18 summers' parenting trend?
cards.body: The trend of turning summer holidays into 'making memories' exercises is overly controlling and misses the point of unstructured time. Long days with nothing planned is what summer should actually be about.

cards.title: My family is coming apart – family games night
cards.body: A parent reflects on 20 years of family life ending, with a final video game session bringing mixed emotions. The piece captures how family dynamics shift as children grow and move on.

cards.title: How to Counter AI Misinformation to Children
cards.body: Children are uniquely vulnerable to digital misinformation, but parents and educators can help them recognize the truth. Proactive approaches are essential in teaching kids to evaluate information critically.

cards.title: Reality and Other Adolescent Worlds
cards.body: Teen fiction reflects the eerie and upside-down world of adolescence, where the boundary between reality and fantasy blurs. Understanding this parallel helps parents and educators support teens navigating identity.

cards.title: Rescue Entitlement Dependency—Is Your Adult Child in RED?
cards.body: Parents often rescue adult children who are 'in the red' financially, but repeated rescue can create unhealthy dependency. Setting boundaries is crucial for healthy adult development.

cards.title: Schools in England have new rules on branded uniforms
cards.body: New regulations limit branded uniform purchases to three items plus a tie for secondary students. The changes aim to reduce financial burden on families.
